scenes.description: Levi Wells, one of the groomsmen, is pacing in the dressing room, wringing his hands and looking increasingly agitated. The other groomsmen, Joe the groom and Lucy the bride, are preparing for the big event. Levi’s dress shoes, which he ordered online, haven’t arrived, and he’s worried it will affect the wedding’s flow.

characters.position: Standing near the mirror, adjusting her veil

actions.dialogue: Hey, guys... I need your help. My dress shoes never arrived, and I don’t have a backup. I feel awful for not being prepared.
Levi, don’t panic. We’ll figure something out. What time were they supposed to be delivered?
They were supposed to be here by noon. I’ve called the store three times, and no one is answering. I’m just... I’m not used to things going wrong like this.
Levi, you’ve always been so reliable and responsible. We can’t let this get to you. Let’s brainstorm solutions.
Maybe we can call the venue and see if they have a pair we can borrow. I know they keep spares for emergencies.
That might work. I just feel so unprepared. I’ve handled event crises before, but this is personal now. I don’t want to mess up.
You’re doing everything you can. That’s what matters. Let’s go find those shoes before the ceremony starts.

scenes.plot: Levi’s missing dress shoes create a last-minute crisis during the wedding preparations. His anxiety and sense of responsibility drive him to seek help from the groom and bride, who support him in finding a solution to ensure the wedding runs smoothly.
scenes.social_purpose: To demonstrate Levi’s traits of anxiety, responsibility, and determination in a high-pressure social setting while showing how the group works together to solve a problem.
